title: POLICE OFFICIALS SERVICE REGULATIONS
full_text:
POLICE OFFICIALS SERVICE REGULATIONS

 

 
 Presidential Decree No. 31380, Jan. 5, 2021 

 

 

 

 Presidential Decree No. 31380, Jan. 5, 2021

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 1 (Purpose)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters relating to the service of police officials.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 2 (Definition)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
The term "police agency" in this Decree means a police agency under 
Article 3
 (2) of the Decree on Disciplinary Action against Police Officials.
[This Article Wholly Amended Nov. 11, 2008]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 3 (Basic principles)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
Police officials shall perform their duties in accordance with the following basic principles: <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021>
1.
 Police mission:
The mission of police officials is to demonstrate allegiance to the State and serve the people, protect lives, bodies, and property, and maintain public well-being and order;
2.
 Police spirit:
Police officials, as those delegated with duties on behalf of the people, shall perform their daily duties based on the principles of national defense, service, and justice while respecting the freedom and rights of the citizens;
3.
 Discipline:
Police officials shall adhere to statutes or regulations, comply with orders issued in the course of performing their duties, and maintain discipline by respecting both their superiors and subordinates;
4.
 Unity:
To accomplish their mission, police officials shall make best efforts to perform their duties with pride while being united;
5.
 Responsibility:
Police officers shall execute their duties with creativity and diligence, and shall be held accountable for the outcomes of their performance;
6.
 Sincerity and integrity:
Police officials shall serve as role models for the public, exemplifying sincerity and integrity.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
CHAPTER II SERVICE ATTITUDES

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 4 (Manners)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Police officials shall endeavor to use polite language and be humble and kind to citizens.
(2)
 Police officials shall adhere to proper etiquette when interacting with superiors, subordinates, and colleagues.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 5 (Appearance and attire)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
Police officials shall maintain their dignity by keeping their appearance and attire neat and presentable.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 6 (Organized environment)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
Police officials shall always keep their office and the surrounding environment neat and tidy, and maintain a cheerful atmosphere.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 7 (Daily behavior)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
Police officials shall set an example for the public in both their public or private lives, and shall adhere to the following standards:
1.
 They shall not criticize, maliciously criticize, quarrel with, or compete against their superiors, subordinates, or colleagues, and shall always demonstrate a spirit of cooperation and camaraderie;
2.
 They shall not engage in frivolous or violent behavior, and shall always be cheerful and lively;
3.
 They shall not engage in any inappropriate entertainment activities.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
CHAPTER III SERVICE

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 8 (Prohibition of performance of duties outside designated places)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
No police official shall perform his or her duties in a place not related to his or her official duties, except with permission from his or her superior or when ordered thereby.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 9 (Prohibition of drinking alcohol during working hours)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
No police official shall consume alcohol during working hours; provided, in unavoidable circumstances where alcohol consumption occurs, he or she shall not perform duties under the influence of alcohol.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 10 (Prohibition of unfair intervention in civil disputes)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
No police official shall unfairly intervene in another person's civil dispute by taking advantage of his or her position or authority.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 11 (Reporting on superiors)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
A police official shall report to his or her superiors regarding any new employment, promotion, transfer, dispatch, business trip, annual leave, admission to an educational and training institution, or any change in status or working relationship.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 12 (Reporting and notification)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
A police official shall promptly, accurately, and concisely report and notify situations necessary for public order.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 13 (Restrictions on travel)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
When a police official intends to travel to an area where it is difficult to return to duty within 2 hours on a holiday or outside working hours, he or she shall file a report with the head of the competent police agency; provided, he or she shall obtain permission from the head of the competent police agency during periods designated by the Commissioner General of the Korean National Police Agency, the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard, or the head of the police agency due to special circumstances with regard to public order. <Amended on Jul. 30, 1991; Nov. 11, 2008; Jul. 26, 2017>

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 14 (Emergency call)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 If the head of a police agency deems it necessary to respond to an emergency, he or she may urgently call police officials under his or her jurisdiction (hereinafter referred to as "emergency call") or have them wait at a specified location.
(2)
 The requirements, types, procedures, and other matters necessary for an emergency call under paragraph (1) shall be determined by the Commissioner General of the Korean National Police Agency or the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard. <Amended on Jul. 30, 1991; Aug. 8, 1996; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 15 (Service rules of special workers)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The Commissioner General of the Korean National Police Agency or the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may separately prescribe and implement matters necessary for the service rules, domestic life, and other aspects of service for police officials whose main duties include counter-espionage operations, maritime police officials of the Korea Coast Guard, members of police squads, and other special police officials. <Amended on Jul. 30, 1991; Jul. 28, 1996; Aug. 8, 1996; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
(2)
 The Commissioner General of the Korean National Police Agency or the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may, if deemed necessary, determine and require the head of the relevant police agency to perform some of the matters necessary for service under paragraph (1). <Amended on Jul. 30, 1991; Aug. 8, 1996; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
CHAPTER IV BOOSTING MORALE AND LEAVES

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 16 (Boosting morale)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
The head of a police agency shall seek to motivate police officials under his or her jurisdiction by means of personnel counseling, grievance handling, and other means, and to boost their morale.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 17 (Health management)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The head of a police agency shall devise measures for maintaining health and improving physical strength of police officials under his or her jurisdiction.
(2)
 A police official shall always pay attention to his or her health and sanitation and endeavor to maintain his or her health and improve his or her physical strength.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 18 (Reward vocation)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
The head of a police agency may grant a reward vocation of up to 10 days to a police official who has an excellent service record or who has rendered distinguished service which can serve as an example for other police officials. In such cases, the reward vacation period shall not be included in the official's annual leave days.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 19 (Leave of absence for day-to-day workers)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
The head of a police agency shall permit the following days off, except in extenuating circumstances: <Amended on November 11, 2008>
1.
 For a day-to-day worker or a worker who works on a public holiday, 1 day off on the following day;
2.
 For a worker on night duty or all-night duty, time off in the morning or afternoon based on 2 p.m. of the following day.
[Title Amended on Nov. 11, 2008]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
CHAPTER V SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 20 (Application mutatis mutandis of the State Public Officials Service Regulations)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
Except as provided in this Decree, the 
State Public Officials Service Regulations
 shall apply to the service of police officials.
[This Article Wholly Amended Nov. 11, 2008]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
ADDENDA <No. 11144, Jun. 11, 1983>

 
(1)
 (Enforcement date) This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.
(2)
 Omitted.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 13435, Jul. 30, 1991>

 
Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Decree shall enter into force on July 31, 1991.
Articles 2
 and 3 Omitted.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 15136, Aug. 8, 1996>

 
Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.
Articles 2
 through 4 Omitted.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
ADDENDUM <Presidential Decree No. 21110, Nov. 11, 2008>

 
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 25751, Nov. 19, 2014>

 
Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation; provided, the amendments to the Presidential Decrees to be amended under 
Article 5
 of the Addenda, which were promulgated before this Decree enters into force but the enforcement dates of which have yet to arrive, shall enter into force on the enforcement date of the relevant Presidential Decree.
Articles 2
 through 5 Omitted.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 28215, Jul. 26, 2017>

 
Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.
Articles 2
 and 3 Omitted.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
ADDENDUM <Presidential Decree No. 31380, Jan. 5, 2021>

 
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation. (Proviso Omitted.)
